check_futures_alerts.description: Ask Kraken which futures contracts are not trading normally right now - one whose price has come adrift of its index, or one moving violently enough for Kraken to have raised the margin behind it. Only the flagged contracts come back, so a scheduled check can branch on 'unusual_activity' instead of reading through several hundred contracts that are fine.
check_futures_alerts.display_str_template: Check Kraken futures for unusual activity.

mock_response.message: All 294 Kraken futures contracts are trading normally.

check_futures_alerts.name: check_futures_alerts

check_status.description: Check whether Kraken is trading, how quickly it is answering, and what maintenance it has announced. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can decide what to do about it - skip a report, wait, or say the figures are stale - rather than dying halfway through.

mock_response.message: Kraken is fully operational. Kraken Website and API Maintenance is scheduled for 2026-09-03T07:01:00Z.

check_status.name: check_status

get_futures_funding_rates.description: See what holding a perpetual contract has cost, hour by hour. Funding is the payment that keeps a perpetual near the spot price: every hour one side pays the other, and a positive rate means the people who are long are paying the people who are short. The average is also given annualised, which is the figure that makes an hourly rate of 0.0005% mean something. Dated futures do not pay funding, and choosing one says so.
get_futures_funding_rates.name: get_futures_funding_rates

parameters.description: Which perpetual contract's funding to read. A dated future has none.
parameters.name: symbol

parameters.description: How many of the most recent hourly rates to return. A day is 24 and a week is 168.
parameters.name: limit

get_futures_order_book.description: See the buy and sell orders waiting on one futures contract, best price first, with the spread and the resting size on each side worked out. Kraken publishes the whole book on the derivatives platform - often more than a thousand levels a side - so 'Price levels' decides how much of the top of it you get back.
get_futures_order_book.display_str_template: Get the Kraken futures order book for {0}.
get_futures_order_book.name: get_futures_order_book

parameters.description: Which contract's order book to read.
parameters.name: symbol

parameters.description: How many price levels to return on each side, starting from the best price.
parameters.name: depth

get_futures_price.description: Get what one or more futures contracts are trading at, with the two numbers only a derivatives market has: the funding rate, which says which side is paying the other to hold the position, and the open interest, which says how much is riding on it. The mark price - what positions are valued and liquidated at - comes back beside the last traded price.
get_futures_price.name: get_futures_price

parameters.description: Which contracts to price. Pick as many as you need; they are fetched together, so ten cost the same as one. At most 20 at a time.
parameters.name: symbols

get_order_book.description: See the buy and sell orders waiting to be filled on one pair, best price first - what it would actually cost to trade a given size, rather than what the last trade happened to go at. The spread between the best bid and the best ask is worked out for you, along with how much is resting on each side.
get_order_book.display_str_template: Get the Kraken order book for {0}.
get_order_book.name: get_order_book

parameters.description: Which pair's order book to read.
parameters.name: pair

parameters.description: How many price levels to return on each side. Ten is enough to see the top of the book; raise it to weigh a larger order against the resting size.
parameters.name: depth

get_price.description: Get what one or more pairs are trading at right now: the last traded price, the best bid and ask, and the day's high, low, volume and change. This is the action for a price alert, a morning summary or a figure to drop into a message. Pick several pairs and they come back in one request.
get_price.name: get_price

parameters.description: Which pairs to price. Pick as many as you need; they are fetched together, so ten pairs cost the same as one. At most 20 at a time.
parameters.name: pairs

get_price_history.description: Get a pair's price as candles - the open, high, low and close of each minute, hour, day or week - for charting, for a moving average, or for comparing today against last month. Kraken is always still filling in the most recent candle, so each one says whether its period has closed: read 'complete' before treating a candle as settled.
get_price_history.name: get_price_history

parameters.description: Which pair's history to read.
parameters.name: pair

parameters.description: How much time each candle covers. Kraken keeps around 720 of them per pair, so an hourly candle reaches back about a month and a daily one about two years.
parameters.name: interval

parameters.description: How many of the most recent candles to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Only candles from this moment onwards. Leave it empty for the most recent ones, which is what a chart or a running average wants.
parameters.name: since

get_spread_history.description: See how the gap between the best bid and the best ask on one pair has moved over the last few minutes, with the narrowest, widest and average across the window. A widening spread is how thin liquidity shows up before it shows up in the price, so this is the one to watch before trading size.
get_spread_history.display_str_template: Get the Kraken spread history for {0}.
get_spread_history.name: get_spread_history

parameters.description: Which pair's spreads to read.
parameters.name: pair

parameters.description: How many of the most recent quote changes to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Only quotes from this moment onwards. Leave it empty for the most recent ones.
parameters.name: since

list_currencies.description: See the coins and currencies Kraken lists, whether each is currently enabled, how many decimal places it holds, and the code it goes by. Worth running once while building: Kraken's API calls bitcoin XBT and dogecoin XDG, and this is where that mapping is visible.
list_currencies.name: list_currencies

parameters.description: Only these currencies. Leave it empty to list every one Kraken holds, which runs to several hundred.
parameters.name: currencies

parameters.description: How many currencies to return, in alphabetical order.
parameters.name: limit

list_futures_contracts.description: See what Kraken's derivatives platform lists and the terms of each contract: its size, its price increment, when it was listed, and - for a dated future - when it stops trading. Filter to perpetuals, which run indefinitely and pay funding, or to dated futures, which expire on a set day.
list_futures_contracts.name: list_futures_contracts

parameters.description: Only these contracts. Leave it empty to list every one Kraken offers.
parameters.name: symbols

parameters.description: Which kind to include. A perpetual never expires and pays funding every hour; a dated future settles on a fixed day and does not.
parameters.name: contract_type

parameters.description: How many contracts to return, in alphabetical order.
parameters.name: limit

list_recent_futures_trades.description: List the fills that have actually happened on one futures contract, oldest first, each with its price, size, side and time. Kraken returns the hundred most recent; to walk further back, set 'Up to' to the earliest time you were given and run it again.
list_recent_futures_trades.display_str_template: List recent Kraken futures trades for {0}.
list_recent_futures_trades.name: list_recent_futures_trades

parameters.description: Which contract's fills to read.
parameters.name: symbol

parameters.description: How many of the most recent fills to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Only fills from before this moment, for stepping back through the history. Leave it empty for the most recent ones.
parameters.name: before

list_recent_trades.description: List the trades that have actually happened on one pair, oldest first, each with its price, size, side and time. This is what really changed hands, as opposed to what is being asked for in the order book. To follow a pair over time, feed 'next_since' from one run into 'Start from' on the next and you pick up exactly where you left off.
list_recent_trades.name: list_recent_trades

parameters.description: Which pair's trades to read.
parameters.name: pair

parameters.description: How many of the most recent trades to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Only trades from this moment onwards. Leave it empty for the most recent ones.
parameters.name: since

list_trading_pairs.description: See what Kraken trades and on what terms: the smallest order it accepts, the smallest order value, the price increment, the standard maker and taker fees, and whether the pair is trading normally or restricted. Filter to one currency to see everything it trades against.
list_trading_pairs.name: list_trading_pairs

parameters.description: Only these pairs. Leave it empty to list everything Kraken trades, which is well over a thousand pairs - so use 'How many' or the currency filter with it.
parameters.name: pairs

parameters.description: Only pairs with this currency on either side: choose USD for every dollar market, or BTC for everything quoted in or against bitcoin.
parameters.name: currency

parameters.description: How many pairs to return, in alphabetical order.
parameters.name: limit

description: Read Kraken's public market data. Get a live price for any of the 1,400-plus pairs it trades, pull candles for a chart or a moving average, look into the order book, follow the trades and the spread, and check whether the exchange is up before you rely on the figures. Kraken's derivatives platform is here too: contract terms, prices, order books, fills, funding rates, and an alert for any contract not trading normally. No API key, no account and no sign-up - and every action reads, so nothing can reach an account or move money.
